concept_html:
A shortcut is a folder in a lakehouse (or KQL database) that points to data somewhere else. It behaves like a symbolic link. The target can be inside OneLake, such as a table in another workspace, or outside it: ADLS Gen2, Azure Blob Storage, Amazon S3 and S3-compatible storage, Google Cloud Storage, Dataverse, OneDrive or SharePoint.

Shortcuts let every Fabric engine read the data without copying it. OneLake handles the connection and credentials, so each workload does not need its own.

Where you create the shortcut matters:

  • Under Tables, point it at Delta data. The lakehouse recognises the folder as a table, and the SQL analytics endpoint and Direct Lake can use it.
  • Under Files, it can point at data in any format.

Deletes are the trap. Microsoft Learn states the rule plainly:

  • Deleting the shortcut itself deletes only the shortcut. The target data stays.
  • Deleting a file or folder inside the shortcut deletes it in the target, if your identity has write permission there.

So a clean-up notebook that runs rm -r on Files/partner_feed/2025/ removes the partner's 2025 files from their storage account, not a local copy.

Other points from Learn (checked September 2026):

  • Moving, renaming or deleting the target breaks the shortcut. Broken shortcuts appear in the Unidentified area.
  • For external shortcuts you can turn on caching. OneLake keeps files it has read for 1 to 28 days, which cuts cross-cloud egress costs.
  • With Direct Lake over SQL or T-SQL in delegated identity mode, the calling user's identity is not passed through to the target. Check which identity reaches the source before relying on its permissions.

def safe_to_delete(path: str, shortcut_roots: set[str]) -> bool:
"""True only for paths this lakehouse owns, never under a shortcut."""
if any(path == root or path.startswith(root.rstrip("/") + "/") for root in shortcut_roots):
return False
return path.startswith(OWNED_PREFIXES)

exercises.solution:
OWNED_PREFIXES = ("Files/landing/", "Files/tmp/")


def safe_to_delete(path: str, shortcut_roots: set[str]) -> bool:
    """True only for owned paths that are not under a shortcut.

    Args:
        path: Lakehouse-relative path, such as Files/landing/w14.csv.
        shortcut_roots: Paths of every shortcut in the lakehouse.

    Returns:
        Whether a clean-up job may delete the path.
    """
    for root in shortcut_roots:
        base = root.rstrip("/")
        if path == base or path.startswith(base + "/"):
            return False
    return path.startswith(OWNED_PREFIXES)

title: OneLake shortcuts, and the delete that goes through
why_html: A lakehouse held a shortcut Files/finance_share to a folder in the finance team's storage account. An analyst ran a notebook to free up space: it deleted every subfolder older than two years under Files/. Their identity had write access to the finance account for another project. Seven years of finance exports disappeared from the source. The storage account had no soft delete, and the files were gone.
